Φαρές.long: Perez, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Φαρές.as:
Φαρές, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פֶּרֶץ, Ge 38:29),
Peres: Mt 1:3, Lk 3:33.†

φαίνω.long: (a) act: I shine, shed light, (b) pass: I shine, become visible, appear, (c) I become clear, appear, seem, show myself as.
φαίνω.sd: to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative)
φαίνω.kj: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think
φαίνω.der: prolongation for the base of G5457 (φῶς);
φαίνω.as:
φαίνω
[in LXX for אור hi., ראה ni., etc. ;]
I. Act.,
1.to bring to light, cause to appear (so most freq. in cl.).
2. Absol., to give light, shine (Hom., Plat., al.): Jo 1:55:35, II Pe 1:19, I Jo 2:8, Re 1:168:1218:2321:23.
II. Pass., to come to light, appear, be manifest: Mt 2:713:2624:27, 30, Lk 9:8, Phl 2:15, He 11:3, I Pe 4:18(LXX); opp. to ἀφανίζεσθαι, Ja 4:14; c. dat. pers. (Bl. § 54, 4), Mt 1:202:13, 19, Mk 16:9; c. nom. pred., Mt 23:27, 28, Ro 7:13, II Co 13:7; id. c. dat. pers., Mt 6:5, 16, 18 (seq. nom. ptcp., but not as in cl.; v. Bl., § 73, 4); impers., Mt 9:33; of the mind and judgment (= δοκεῖ, q.v.), Mk 14:64 (cf. I Es 2:21), Lk 24:11.†
SYN.: v.s. δοκέω

φοβέομαι.long: I fear, dread, reverence, am afraid, terrified.
φοβέομαι.sd: to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere
φοβέομαι.as:
φοβέω, ῶ
(< φόβος) [in LXX chiefly for ירא ;]
1. in Hom., to put to flight. Pass., to be put to flight, to flee affrighted
2.to terrify, frighten (Wis 179; Hdt. and Att..). Pass. (so always in NT; cf. M, Pr., 162), to be seized with fear, be affrighted, fear: Mt 10:3114:27, Mk 5:336:50, Lk 1:138:50, Jo 6:1912:15, Ac 16:38, al.; opp. to ὑψηλοφρονεῖν, Ro 11:20; σφόδρα, Mt 17:627:54; c. cogn. acc., φόβον μέγαν, Mk 4:41, Lk 2:9 (I Mac 10:8); φόβον αὐτῶν (obj, gen., but cf. ICC, in l.), I Pe 3:14; πτόησιν, I Pe 3:6; c. acc. pers., Mt 10:26, Mk 11:18, Lk 19:21, Jo 9:22, Ac 9:26,
Ro 13:3, al.; seq. ἀπό (like Heb. יָרֵא, Je 1:8, al.; cf. M, Pr., 102, 104n), Mt 10:28, Lk 12:4; seq. μή (cl.; Bl., § 65, 3; M, Pr., 184 f.), Ac 23:1027:17; μήπως, Ac 27:29, II Co 11:312:20, Ga 4:11; μήποτε, He 4:1; c. inf. (Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 205), Mt 1:20, Mk 9:32, al.; of reverential fear: Mk 6:20, Eph 5:33; τ. θεόν, Lk 1:50, Ac 10:2, I Pe 2:17, Re 14:7, al.; τ. κύριον, Col 3:22, Re 15:4; τ. ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ (v.s. ὄνομα), Re 11:18; οἱ φοβούμενοι τ. θεόν, of proselytes, Ac 13:16, 26 (cf. ἐκ-φοβέω)

φεύγω.sd: to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish
φεύγω.as:
φεύγω
[in LXX chiefly for נוּס, also for בּרח, etc. ;]
to flee from or away, take flight: absol., Mt 8:3326:56, Mk 5:1414:50, Lk 8:34, Jo 10:12, Ac 7:29; seq. εἰς, Mt 2:1310:2324:16 (WH, txt.), Mk 13:14, Lk 21:21, Re 12:6; ἐπί, c. acc. loc., Mt 24:16 (WH, mg.); ἐκ, Ac 27:30; ἀπό, c. gen. loc. (cl.), Mk 16:8; id. c. gen. pers. (as in Heb.), Jo 10:5, Ja 4:7. Metaph.: absol., Re 16:20; c. acc. rei, I Co 6:18, He 11:34 (v. M, Pr., 116); opp. to διώκειν, I Ti 6:11, II Ti 2:22; seq. ἀπό, c. gen. pers., Re 9:6; ἀπὸ τ. προσώπου, Re 20:11; c. gen. rei, Mt 3:7 (M, Pr., l.c.) 23:33, Lk 3:7, I Co 10:14 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-φεύγω).†

φωνή.long: a sound, noise, voice, language, dialect.
φωνή.sd: a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language
φωνή.der: probably akin to G5316 (φαίνω) through the idea of disclosure;
φωνή.as:
φωνή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for קוֺל ;]
a voice;
(a) prop., of persons, Mt 2:18(LXX), al.; φ. αἴρειν (ἐπαίρειν), Lk 17:13, Ac 2:14, al.; φ. μεγάλῃ εἰπεῖν (λέγειν, φωνεῖν, etc.), Lk 8:28, Ac 7:57, Re 5:12, al.; γίνεται (ἔρχεται) φ. ἐκ τ. οὐρανῶν (ἐξ οὐρανοῦ), Mk 1:11, Lk 3:22, Jo 12:28, al. (cf. DCG, ii, 810a; Dalman, Words, 204 f.); ἀκούειν φωνήν (-ῆς; v.s. ἀκούω), Ac 9:4, 7 al.; φ. βοῶντος, Mt 3:3, Mk 1:3, Lk 3:4, Jo 1:23(LXX); τ. θεοῦ, Jo 5:37, He 3:7, al. By meton.,
(α) of the speaker, βλέπειν τὴν φ., Re 1:12;
(β)speech, language ( Ge 11:1, IV Mac 12:7, al.): I Co 14:10;
(b) of inanimate things: Mt 24:31, Jo 3:8, Ac 2:6, Re 1:15b9:914:2, al. (cf. Tr., Syn., § lxxxix).

Φαρισαῖος.long: a Pharisee, one of the Jewish sect so called.
Φαρισαῖος.sd: a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary
Φαρισαῖος.as:
Φαρισαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. פְּרִישָׁא; v. Dalman, Gr., 157n, Words, 2n),
a Pharisee: Mt 23:26, Phl 3:5; usually in pl., Mt 9:11, Mk 2:18, al.; Φ. κ. γραμματεῖς, Mt 5:20, Mk 2:16, Lk 5:21, al.; Φ. κ. Σαδδυκαῖοι, Mt 16:1, Ac 23:6, 7 al.; ἀρχιερεῖς, Mt 21:45, Jo 7:32, al. (v. DB, iii, 826b).

φημί.sd: to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say
φημί.der: properly, the same as the base of G5457 (φῶς) and G5316 (φαίνω);
φημί.as:
φημί
[in LXX chiefly for נאם, also for אמר; freq. in II-IV Mac ;]
to declare, say: freq. in quoting the words of another, Mt 13:2926:61, Lk 7:4022:58, Jo 1:23, al.; interjected into the recorded words (cl.), Mt 14:8, Ac 23:35, al.; φησί, impersonal (Bl., § 30, 4), I Co 6:16 (Lft., Notes, 217; but cf. Bl., l.c.), II Co 10:10 (WH, mg., φασίν), He 8:5; joined with synon. verb (cf. LS, s.v., II, 2), ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη, Lk 23:3; seq. πρός, Lk 22:70, al.; c. acc rei, I Co 10:1510:19; acc. et inf., Ro 3:8; seq. ὅτι (Bl., § 70, 3), I Co 10:1915:50 (cf. σύν-φημι)

φῶς.long: light, a source of light, radiance.
φῶς.sd: compare G5316 (φαίνω), G5346 (φημί)); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative)
φῶς.der: from an obsolete (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays;
φῶς.as:
φῶς (Att.. contr. from φάος; < φάω), gen., φωτός, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for אוֹר ;]
light (opp. to τὸ σκότος, ἡ σκοτία): Mt 17:2, 5, Jo 11:9, 10, II Co 4:6; ἡλίου, Re 22:5; of a lamp, Lk 8:1611:33, Jo 5:35, Re 18:23; of a supernatural heavenly light, Ac 9:312:722:6, 9, 1126:13; hence, ἄγγελος φωτός, II Co 11:14; ὁ κλήρος τ. ἁγίων ἐν τ. φ., Col 1:12; of the divine glory, Re 21:24; by meton., of that which gives light: of fire, Mk 14:54, Lk 22:56 (cl.; I Mac 12:29; cf. DCG, i, 595); pl., of a lamp or torch, Ac 16:29; of heavenly bodies, Ja 1:17.
Metaph.,
(a) of God: I Jo 1:5, 7; φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, I Ti 6:16;
(b) of spiritual truth and its effects on the lives of men: Mt 4:165:16, Jo 1:4, 53:19-21, Ac 26:18, 23, II Co 6:14, Eph 5:13, I Pe 2:9, I Jo 2:8; τ. φ. τ. ζωῆς, Jo 8:12; τ. ὅπλα τοῦ φ., Ro 13:12; καρπὸς τοῦ φ., Eph 5:9; έν τ. φ. περιπατεῖν (εἶναι, μένειν), I Jo 1:72:9, 10; υἱοὶ (τέκνα) τοῦ φ., Lk 16:8, Jo 12:36, Eph 5:8, I Th 5:5; by meton., of one from whom truth shines forth: Ac 13:47(LXX), Ro 2:19; esp. of Christ, Lk 2:32, Jo 1:7, 812:35, 36, 46; τ. φ. τ. κόσμου, Jo 8:129:5;τ. φ. τ. ἀληθινόν, Jo 1:9; of Christians, Mt 5:14, Eph 5:8;
(c) of the spiritual under­standing: τ. φ. τὸ ἐν σοί, Mt 6:23, Lk 11:35;
(d) adverbially, of that which is open to view (opp. to ἐν τ. σκοτίᾳ): ἐν τ. φ., Mt 10:27, Lk 12:3.†
SYN.: v.s. φέγγος

φονεύω.as:
φονεύω
(< φονεύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָצַח ;]
to kill, murder. absol., Mt 5:21, Ja 4:2; μὴ (οὐ) φονεύσῃς (-εις), Mt 5:2119:18, Mk 10:19, Lk 18:20, Ro 13:9, Ja 2:11 (all from Ex 20:13, 14); c. acc., Mt 23:31, 35, Ja 5:6.†

φυλακή.long: a watching, keeping guard; a guard, prison; imprisonment.
φυλακή.sd: a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively
φυλακή.as:
φυλακή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< φυλάσσω) [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁמֶרֶת and cogn. forms, also for כֶּלֶא etc. ;]
(a) actively, a guarding, guard, watch (Hom., Plat., Xen., al.): cogn. acc., φυλάσσειν φυλακάς, to keep watch, Lk 2:8;
(b) of those who keep watch (as also Lat. custodia), a guard; pl., sentinels, a guard (Hom., al.): Ac 12:10;
(c) of the place where persons are kept under guard, a prison (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Mt 14:10, Mk 6:17, Lk 3:20, Ac 5:19, II Co 6:5, I Pe 3:19, Re 18:2, al.;
(d) of the time during which guard was kept by night (Lat. vigilia; Anthol.), a watch: Mt 14:2524:43, Mk 6:48, Lk 12:38

φιλέω.long: I love (of friendship), regard with affection, cherish; I kiss.
φιλέω.sd: to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while G25 (ἀγαπάω) is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as G2309 (θέλω) and G1014 (βούλομαι), or as G2372 (θυμός) and G3563 (νοῦς) respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness)
φιλέω.as:
φιλέω, -ῶ
(< φίλος), [in LXX: Ge 27:4, 9, al. (אהב), ib. 27, al. (נשׁק), La 1:2 (רֵעַ) Wi 8:2, al. ;]
1.to love (with the love of emotion and friendship, Lat, amare; v. SYN.): c. acc. pers., Mt 10:37, Jo 5:20; Jo 11:3, 3615:1916:2720:221:15-17, I Co 16:22, Re 3:19; ἐν πίστει, Tit 3:15; c. acc. rei, Mt 23:6, Lk 20:46, Jo 12:25, Re 22:15; c. inf. (Is 56:10; cf. Bl., § 69, 4), Mt 6:5.
2.to kiss: c. acc. pers., Mt 26:48, Mk 14:44, Lk 22:47 (cf. κατα-φιλέω).†
SYN.: ἀγαπάωω (q.v.), the love of duty and respect

φωτεινός.as:
** φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν
(< φῶς), [in LXX: Si 17:3123:19 * ;]
bright, light: νεφέλη, Mt 17:5; opp. to σκοτεινός, Mt 6:22, Lk 11:34, 36.†

φρόνιμος.sd: thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while G4680 (σοφός) denotes practical skill or acumen; and G4908 (συνετός) indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative)
φρόνιμος.as:
φρόνιμος, -ον
(< φρονέω), [in LXX for נָבוֺן, חָכָם etc. ;]
practically wise, sensible, prudent: Mt 10:1624:45, Lk 12:42, I Co 10:15; opp. to μωρός, Mt 7:2425:2, 4, 8, 9, I Co 4:10; to ἄφρων, II Co 11:19; φ. παρ’ ἑαυτῷ (EV, wise in one's own conceit), Ro 11:2512:16 (cf. Pr 3:7); compar., -ώτερος, Lk 16:8.†
SYN.: v.s. σοφός

φωλεός.as:
* φωλεός, -οῦ ὁ
a hole, den, lair: Mt 8:20, Lk 9:58.†

φήμη.as:
φήμη, -ης, ἡ
(< φημί) [in LXX: Pr 16:2 (15:30) (שְׁמוּעָה), II Mac 4:39, III Mac 3:2, IV Mac 4:22 * ;]
a saying or report: Mt 9:26, Lk 4:14.†

Φίλιππος.long: Philip, (a) one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, (b) tetrarch of the Ituraean and Trachonitic region, half-brother of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, (c) one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem and a missionary.
Φίλιππος.sd: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites
Φίλιππος.as:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
1. the husband of Herodias: Mt 14:3, Mk 6:17.
2. The tetrarch: Mt 16:13, Mk 8:27, Lk 3:1.
3. The apostle: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:18, Lk 6:14, Jo 1:44-496:5, 712:21, 2214:8, 9, Ac 1:13.
4. The deacon and evangelist: Ac 6:58:5-4021:8.†

φορέω.sd: to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment
φορέω.as:
φορέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Pr 16:23 (יָסַף hi.), Si 11:5, al. ;]
frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action (cf. Tr., Syn., § lviii), most commonly used of clothing, weapons, etc., to bear constantly, wear: Mt 11:8, Jo 19:5, Ro 13:4, I Co 15:49, Ja 2:3.†

φάγος.as:
*† φάγος, -ου, ὁ
(< φαγεῖν, v.s. ἐσθίω)
a glutton: Mt 11:19, Lk 7:34.†

φίλος.long: friendly; subst: a friend, an associate.
φίλος.sd: actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.)
φίλος.as:
φίλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ, אֹהֵב ;]
1. pass., beloved, dear (Hom., Eur., al.).
2. Act., loving, friendly (in cl. less freq. and only in poets): Ac 19:31. As subst., a friend;
(a) masc., ὁ φ.: Lk 7:611:514:1015:616:921:1623:12, Ac 27:3, III Jo 15; opp. to δοῦλος, Jo 15:15; φ. ἀναγκαῖοι, Ac 10:24; c. gen. subj., Mt 11:19, Lk 7:3411:6, 812:414:1215:29, Jo 11:1115:13, 14; ὁ φ. τοῦ νυμφίου, Jo 3:29; τ. Καίσαρος (v. Deiss., BS 167; LAE, 382 f.), Jo 19:12; θεοῦ (v. Hort, in l.), Ja 2:23; c. gen. rei, τ, κόσμου, Ja 4:4;
(b) fem., ἡ φ., Lk 15:9,†

φορτίζω.long: I load, burden; pass: I am laden.
φορτίζω.sd: to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety)
φορτίζω.as:
φορτίζω
(< φόρτος), [in LXX: Ez 16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;]
to load: c. dupl. acc., Lk 11:46; pass., to be laden: metaph. (EV, heavy laden), Mt 11:28.†

φορτίον.long: a burden; the freight of a ship.
φορτίον.sd: an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service
φορτίον.as:
φορτίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of φόρτος), [in LXX chiefly for מַשָּׂא ;]
a burden, load: of the cargo of a ship (Hdt., al.), Ac 27:10; metaph., Mt 11:3023:4, Lk 11:46, Ga 6:5.†
SYN.: βάρος (q.v.), ὄγκος

φανερός.long: apparent, clear, visible, manifest; adv: clearly.
φανερός.sd: shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally
φανερός.kj: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly)
φανερός.as:
φανερός, -ά, -όν
(< φαίνομαι) [in LXX: De 29:29(28) (גּלה ni.), Pr 14:4, Si 6:22, al. ;]
open to sight, visible, manifest: Ga 5:19; seq. ἐν, Ro 1:19, I Jo 3:10; c. dat. pers., Ac 4:167:13, I Ti 4:15; φ. γίνεσθαι (in LXX for בּחן ni., Ge 42:16), Mk 6:14, Lk 8:17, I Co 3:1314:25; id. seq. ἐν, I Co 11:19, Phl 1:13; φ. ποιεῖν, Mt 12:16, Mk 3:12; εἰς φ. ἐλθεῖν (cf. Bl., § 47, 2), Mk 4:22, Lk 8:17; ἐν τῷ φ. (opp. to ἐν τ. κρυπτῷ), Ro 2:28.†
SYN.: v.s. δῆλος

φθάνω.long: (a) I anticipate, precede, (b) I come, arrive.
φθάνω.sd: to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at
φθάνω.as:
φθάνω
[in LXX for נגע hi., מטא, etc. ;]
1.to come before another, anticipate (cl.): c. acc. pers., I Th 4:15.
2. In late writers and MGr. (v. Kennedy, Sources, 156; Lft., Notes, 35), to come, arrive: Ro 9:31; seq. εἰς, Phl 3:16; ἄχρι, II Co 10:14; ἐπί (cf. Da TH 4:21, and v. Dalman, Words, 107), Mt 12:28, Lk 11:20, I Th 2:16 (cf. προ-φθάνω).†

φέρω.long: I carry, bear, bring; I conduct, lead; perhaps: I make publicly known.
φέρω.sd: to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows)
φέρω.kj: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold
φέρω.der: a primary verb (for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, ; and ;
φέρω.as:
φέρω
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא. hi., also for נשׂא, etc. ;]
to bear;
1.to bear, carry: c. acc, Lk 23:2624:1, Jo 19:39, He 1:3 (v. Westc., in l.); pass., Ac 2:227:15, 17He 6:1, II Pe 1:17, 18; of the mind, II Pe 1:21.
2.to bear, endure: c. acc. rei, He 12:2013:13; c. acc pers., Ro 9:22.
3.to bring, bring forward: c. acc. pers., Ac 5:16; id. seq. πρός, Mk 1:322:39:17, 19, 20; ἐπί, Lk 5:18; c. dat., Mk 7:328:22; c. acc. rei, Mk 6:2711:212:15, Lk 15:23, Ac 4:34, 375:2, II Ti 4:13; id. seq. πρός, Mk 11:7; εἰς, Re 21:24, 26; ἐπί, Mt 14:11, Mk 6:28; ἀπό, Jo 21:10; c. dat., Mk 12:15, Jo 2:8; id. seq. ὧδε, Mt 14:1817:17; seq. φαγεῖν (sc. τι), Jo 4:33; τ. δάκτυλον (χεῖρα), Jo 20:27; pass., ἡ χάρις, I Pe 1:13; διδαχήν, II Jo 10; θάνατον (cf. Field, Notes, 230), He 9:16; κρίσιν, II Pe 2:11; κατηγορίαν, Jo 18:29; αἰτίαν, Ac 25:18; αἰτιώματα, ib. 7, Rec.
4.to bear, produce, bring forth: καρπόν, Mt 7:18, Mk 4:8, Jo 12:2415:2, 4, 5, 8, 16.
5.to bring, lead: Mk 15:22, Jo 21:18, Ac 14:13; metaph., of a gate (ὁδός, cl.), Seq. εἰς, Ac 12:10
(cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, εἰσ-, παρ-εισ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-φέρω).†
SYN: φορέω, which expresses habitual and continuous bearing as distinct from (φέρω) that which is accidental and temporary (cf. Mt 11:8, al., s.v. φορέω, and v. Tr., Syn., § lviii)

φάντασμα.as:
φάντασμα, -τος, τό
(< φαντάζω), [in LXX: Jb 20:8 A (חִזָּיוֹן), Is 28:7 A, Wi 17:15 * ;]
= φάσμα, an appearance, apparition (Æsch., al.): Mt 14:26, Mk 6:49 (v. DCG, i, 111b).†

φόβος.long: (a) fear, terror, alarm, (b) the object or cause of fear, (c) reverence, respect.
φόβος.der: from a primary (to be put in fear);
φόβος.as:
φόβος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יִרְאָה, also for פַּחַד, אֵימָה, etc. ;]
1. in Hom., flight.
2. That which causes flight, fear, dread, terror: Lk 1:12, Ac 5:5, I Ti 5:20. I Jo 4:18, al.; cogn. acc., φοβεῖσθαι φ., Mk 4:41, Lk 2:9; c. gen. obj., Jo 7:1319:3320:19, He 2:5, I Pe 3:14 (but cf. ICC, in l.);ἀπὸ (τοῦ) φ., Mt 14:26, Lk 21:26; εἰς φ., Ro 8:15; μετὰ φόβου, Mt 28:8; φ. καὶ τρόμος (Lft., Notes, 172), I Co 2:3, II Co 7:15, Eph 6:5, Phl 2:12; by meton., of that which causes fear, Ro 13:3; of reverential fear, Ro 13:7, I Pe 1:172:183:2, 15; τ. κυρίου, Ac 9:31, II Co 5:11 (v. Field, Notes, 183); Χριστοῦ, Eph 5:21; θεοῦ, Ro 3:18, II Co 7:1
SYN.: v.s. δειλία (and of. DCG, i, 381)

φυτεία.long: a plant, that which is planted.
φυτεία.sd: trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable
φυτεία.as:
φυτεία, -ας, ἡ
(< φυτεύω), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:29 (נטע), Mi 1:6, Ez 17:7 (מַטָּע) * ;]
1.a planting (Xen., al.; LXX).
2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.): Mt 15:13.†

φυτεύω.sd: to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine
φυτεύω.as:
φυτεύω
(< φυτόν, a plant, < φύω), [in LXX chiefly for נטע, also for שׁתל, etc. ;]
to plant: Lk 17:28, I Co 3:6-8; c. acc., φυτείαν, Mt 15:13; ἀμπελῶνα, Mt 21:33, Mk 12:1, Lk 20:9, I Co 9:7; pass., seq. ἐν, Lk 13:617:6.†

φράζω.sd: to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound
φράζω.der: probably akin to G5420 (φράσσω) through the idea of defining;
φράζω.as:
φράζω
[in LXX: Jb 6:24 (בִּין hi.) Jb 12:8 (יָרָה hi.), Da LXX 2:4 (חָוָה pa.) * ;]
to show forth, tell, declare, explain: Mt 13:36 (WH, RV, διασάφησον) 15:15.†

φόνος.as:
φόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for דָּם, פֶּה, etc. ;]
murder, slaughter: Mk 15:7, Lk 23:19, 25, Ac 9:1, Ro 1:29; φ. μαχαίρης (cf. Ex 17:13, al.), He 11:37; pl., Mt 15:19, Mk 7:21, Re 9:21.†

φρονέω.long: (a) I think, (b) I think, judge, (c) I direct the mind to, seek for, (d) I observe, (e) I care for.
φρονέω.sd: to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience)
φρονέω.kj: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think
φρονέω.as:
φρονέω, -ῶ
(< φρήν), [in LXX: De 32:29, Za 9:2 (חָכָם), Ps 93 (94):8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Is 44:18 (בִּין) ib. 28, Es 8:13, Wi 1:114:30, I Mac 10:20, II Mac 9:12; 14:8, 26 * ;]
1.to have understanding (Hom., al.).
2.to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, I Co 13:11; c. acc. (usually neut., adj., or pron., as freq. in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Ro 12:3; ἃ, Ac 28:22; τοῦτο, Phl 3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Ga 5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, II Co 13:11, Phl 2:24:2; id. seq. εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Ro 12:1615:5; τ. ἓν φ., Phl 2:2 (Lft., in l.); seq. ὑπέρ, Phl 1:7.
3.to have in mind, be mindful of, think of (Hdt., Xen., al.; Es, 1Mac, ll. c.): τὰ τ. θεοῦ, opp. to τ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Mt 16:23, Mk 8:33; τὰ τ. σαρκός, opp. to τ. τ. πνεύρατος, Ro 8:5; τ. ἐπίγεια, Phl 3:19; τὰ ἄνω, opp. to τ. ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, Col 3:2; τοῦτο φρονεῖτε (RV, have this mind in you), Phl 2:5; ὑψηλά, Ro 12:16; φ. ἡμέραν (to observe a day), Ro 14:6; seq. ὑπέρ, Phl 4:10 (cf. κατα-, παρα-, περι-, ὑπερ-φρσνέω).†

φυλάσσω.long: (a) I guard, protect; mid: I am on my guard, (b) act. and mid. of customs and regulations: I keep, observe.
φυλάσσω.sd: to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid
φυλάσσω.der: probably from G5443 (φυλή) through the idea of isolation;
φυλάσσω.as:
φυλάσσω
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for שָׁמַר, also for נָצַר, etc. ;]
to guard, watch;
(a)to guard or watch: c. cogn. acc., φυλακάς, Lk 2:8; c. acc. pers., Ac 12:428:16; pass., Lk 8:29, Ac 23:35; c. acc. rei, Ac 22:20;
(b)to guard or protect: c. acc., Lk 11:21, Jo 12:2517:12, II Th 3:3, I Ti 6:20, II Ti 1:12, 14, II Pe 2:5; ἑαυτὸν ἀπό, I Jo 5:21 (Westc., in l.); metaph. of law, precept, etc., to keep, preserve, observe: Mt 19:20, Lk 11:2818:21, Jo 12:47, Ac 7:5316:421:24, Ro 2:26, Ga 6:13, I Ti 5:21. Mid., to be on one's guard (against), keep oneself from, beware of: c. acc., Ac 21:25, II Ti 4:15; seq. ἀπό., Lk 12:15; ἵνα μή, II Pe 3:17; as in LXX (Ex 12:17, Le 18:4, al.), of laws, etc., to keep, observe: ταῦτα πάντα, Mk 10:20 (cf. δια-φυάσσω).†
SYN.: τηρέω, q.v

φυλή.long: a tribe or race of people.
φυλή.sd: an offshoot, i.e. race or clan
φυλή.as:
φυλή, ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for; מַטֶּה, also for שֵׁבֶט, מִשְׁפָּחָה, etc. ;]
a body of men united by kinship or habitation, a clan or tribe: of the tribes of Israel, Mt 19:28, Lk 2:3622:30, Ac 13:21, Ro 11:1, Phl 3:5, He 7:13, 14, Ja 1:1, Re 5:57:4-821:12; of the tribes of the earth, the peoples and nations, Mt 24:30, Re 1:75:97:911:913:714:6.†

φωνέω.long: I give forth a sound, hence: (a) of a cock: I crow, (b) of men: I shout, (c) trans: I call (to myself), summon; I invite, address.
φωνέω.sd: to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation
φωνέω.as:
φωνέω, -ῶ
(< φωνή), [in LXX for קרא (Je 17:11, al.), etc. ;]
I. Intrans.
1. Of persons, to call out, cry out, speak aloud: Lk 8:8; φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, Mk 1:26, Ac 16:28; ἐφώνησε (φωνῇ μεγάλῇ) λέγων, Lk 8:54, Re 14:18; φωνήσαντες ἐπύθοντο, Ac 10:18.
2. Of the cries of animals (rarely in cl.; Is 38:14, Je, l.c.): of a cock, to crow, Mt 263, Mk 14, Lk 223, Jo 13:3818:27.
II. Trans. (in cl. chiefly poët.), c. acc. pers., to call, summon, invite: Mt 20:3227:47, Mk 9:3510:4915:35, Lk 14:1216:219:15, Jo 1:492:94:1610:311:2812:1718:33, Ac 9:4110:7; to address, call by name (Soph.), Jo 13:13 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπι-, προσ-, συν-φωνέω).†

φύλλον.as:
φύλλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for עָלֶה ;]
a leaf: Mt 21:1924:32, Mk 11:1313:28, Re 22:2.†

φραγμός.sd: a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively)
φραγμός.as:
φραγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< φράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for גָּדֵר, גְּדֵרָה, also for פֶּרֶץ, etc. ;]
1. prop., a fencing in (Soph., OT, 1387).
2. = φράγμα, a fence: Mt 21:33, Mk 12:1, Lk 14:23. Metaph., μεσότοιχον (q.v.) τοῦ φ., gen. epexeg., Eph 2:14 (v. Ellic., in l.).†

φονεύς.sd: a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which G443 (ἀνθρωποκτόνος) does not necessarily imply; while G4607 (σικάριος) is a special term for a public bandit)
φονεύς.as:
* φονεύς, -έως, ὁ
(φόνος) [in LXX: Wi 12:5 * ;]
a murderer: Mt 22:7Ac 7:5228:4, I Pe 4:15, Re 21:822:15; ἀνὴρ φ., Ac 3:14.†
SYN.: ἀνθρωποκτόνος

φιμόω.as:
φιμόω, -ῶ
(< φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: De 25:4 (חסם), Da LXX Su 1:61, IV Mac 1:35א R * ;]
to muzzle: I Co 9:9, I Ti 5:18(LXX); metaph., to put to silence: c. acc. pers., Mt 22:34, I Pe 2:15; pass., to be silenced, silent: Mt 22:12, Mk 1:254:39, Lk 4:35.†

φυλακτήριον.long: a phylactery, an amulet, a parchment capsule containing little parchment rolls with the Hebrew texts, affixed to the left upper arm or the forehead of men at morning prayer, and regarded as a protection (hence the name) against evil spirits.
φυλακτήριον.sd: a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts
φυλακτήριον.der: neuter of a derivative of G5442 (φυλάσσω);
φυλακτήριον.as:
* φυλακτήριον, -ου, τό
1.an outpost, fortification (Thuc., al.).
2.a safeguard (Plat.).
3.an amulet (Plut., al.); in NT for the Talmudic תְּפִלִּין, a prayer fillet, a phylactery, a small strip of parchment on which portions of the law were written and worn on the forehead and next the heart (cf. Ex 13:16): Mt 23:5.†

φυγή.as:
φυγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< φεύγω), [in LXX chiefly for מָנוֹס and cogn. forms ;]
flight: Mt 24:20.†

φέγγος.der: probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς) (compare G5350 (φθέγγομαι));
φέγγος.as:
φέγγος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for נֹגַהּ ;]
light, brightness, usually c. gen. of something that shines or reflects: of the moon, Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24; of a lamp, Lk 11:33 (WH, RV, φῶς).†
SYN.: αὐγή, q.v.

φθόνος.der: probably akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω);
φθόνος.as:
** φθόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Wi 2:246:23, I Mac 8:16, III Mac 6:7 * ;]
envy: Ro 1:29, Ga 5:21, I Ti 6:4, Tit 3:3, I Pe 2:1; διὰ φθόνον, Mt 27:18, Mk 15:10, Phl 1:15; πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τ. πνεῦμα (on the meaning, v. R, txt., mg. 1, 2; Hort, Ja., 93 f.), Ja 4:5.†

φραγελλόω.sd: to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment
φραγελλόω.der: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum;
φραγελλόω.as:
*† φραγελλόω, -ῶ
(< φραγέλλιον, q.v.),
to scourge: c. acc., Mt 27:26, Mk 15:15 (eccl.).†

φανερῶς.as:
** φανερῶς
adv.
(< φανερός), [in LXX: II Mac 3:28 * ;]
(a)manifestly, openly: Mk 1:45; opp. to ἐν κρυπτῷ„ Jo 7:10;
(b)clearly: Ac 10:3 (II Mac 3:28).†

φανερόω.g: I make clear, visible, or manifest
φανερόω.long: I make clear (visible, manifest), make known.
φανερόω.as:
φανερόω, -ώ
[in LXX: Je 40 (33):6 (גּלה pi.) * ;]
to make visible, clear, manifest or known: c. acc rei, Jo 2:1117:6, Ro 1:19, I Co 4:5, II Co 2:1411:6, Col 4:4, Tit 1:3; pass., Mk 4:22, Jo 3:219:3, Ro 3:2116:26, II Co 4:10, 11, Eph 5:13, Col 1:26, II Ti 1:10, He 9:8, I Jo 3:24:9, Re 3:1815:4; c. acc pers., of Christ, Jo 7:421:1; pass., II Co 3:35:10, 11, I Jo 2:19; of Christ, Mk 16:12, 14, Jo 1:3121:14, Col 3:4, I Ti 3:16, He 9:26, I Pe 1:205:4, I Jo 1:2 (ἡ ζωή; v. Westc., in l.) 2:283:2, 5, 8.†
SYN.: v.s. ἀποκαλύπτω

φρόνησις.long: understanding (which leads to right action), practical wisdom, prudence.
φρόνησις.sd: mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight
φρόνησις.as:
φρόνησις, -εως, ἡ
(< φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּינָה, תְּבוּנָה, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;]
understanding, practical wisdom, prudence: Lk 1:17, Eph 1:8.†
SYN.: v.s. σοφία, and cf. Lft., Notes, 317.

φάτνη.as:
φάτνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for אֵבוּס, etc. ;]
a manger: Lk 2:7, 12, 1613:15 (v. DB, iii, 234a, DCG, ii, 111a),†

Φανουήλ.long: Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.

φάραγξ.sd: a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent)
φάραγξ.der: properly, strengthened from the base of G4008 (πέραν) or rather of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι);
φάραγξ.as:
φάραγξ, -αγγος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for נַחַל, also for גַּיְא, etc. ;]
a chasm, ravine: Lk 3:5(LXX) (v. DB, iv, 845 f.).†

Φάλεκ.long: Peleg, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Φάλεκ.as:
Φάλεκ (T, Rec. Φαλέκ, L, mg., Φάλεγ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. פָּלֶג, Ge 11:16),
Peleg: Lk 3:35.†

φίλημα.as:
φίλημα, -τος, τό
(< φιλέω), [in LXX: Pr 27:6, Ca 1:2 (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;]
a kiss: Lk 7:4522:48; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, Ro 16:16, I Co 16:20, II Co 13:12, I Th 5:26; φ. ἀγάπης, I Pe 5:14 (v. Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, s.v. "Kiss").†

φύω.long: I grow, grow up, spring up.
φύω.sd: probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively
φύω.as:
φύω
[in LXX: Pr 26:9, Ez 37:8 (עלה), etc. ;]
1. trans., to bring forth, produce (of men, to beget); pass., to spring up, grow: Lk 8:6, 8.
2. Intrans., in 2 aor., pf., plpf., and rarely in pres. (v. LS, s.v., A, II.), to spring up: He 12:15.†

φωτίζω.long: (a) I light up, illumine, (b) I bring to light, make evident, reveal.
φωτίζω.sd: to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively)
φωτίζω.kj: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see
φωτίζω.as:
φωτίζω
(< φῶς) [in LXX for אוֹר hi, ירה hi., etc. ;]
1. intrans., to shine, give light (Arist., Plut., a1.): seq. ἐπί, Re 22:5.
2. Trans.
(a)to illumine, enlighten (Diod., Plut., al.): c. acc., Lk 11:36, Re 21:23; pass., Re 18:1. Metaph., of spiritual enlightenment (Ps 118 (119):130, Si 45:17, al.): Jo 1:9, Eph 1:183:9, R, txt., He 6:410:32;
(b)to bring to light, make known (Polyb.): I Co 4:5, Eph 3:9, R, mg., II Ti 1:10 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 107 f.).†

φρέαρ.sd: a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison)
φρέαρ.as:
φρέαρ, -ατος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for בְּאֵר ;]
a well: Lk 14:5, Jo 4:11, 12; φ. τῆς ἀβύσσου, Re 9:1, 2.†

φιλάργυρος.as:
** φιλ-άργυρος, -ον
[in LXX: IV Mac 2:8 * ;]
loving money, avaricious: Lk 16:14, II Ti 3:2.†

φλόξ.as:
φλόξ gen., φλογός,
[in LXX chiefly for לַהַב, לֶהָבָה ;]
a flame: Lk 16:24; φ, πυρός, Ac 7:30, II Th 1:8, He 1:7(LXX), Re 1:142:1819:12.†

φόρος.long: a tax, tribute, especially on persons.
φόρος.sd: a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 (τέλος) is usually a general toll on goods or travel)
φόρος.as:
φόρος, -ου, ὁ
(< φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה, etc. ;]
tribute paid by a subject nation (cf. I Mac 10:33): φ. δοῦναι (I Mac 8:4, 7), Lk 20:2223:2; ἀποδοῦναι, Ro 13:7; τελεῖν, Ro 13:6 (Hdt., al.).†
SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος (q.v.)

φόβητρον.long: a terrible sight, cause of terror, an object of fear.
φόβητρον.sd: a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent
φόβητρον.der: neuter of a derivative of G5399 (φοβέω);
φόβητρον.as:
φόβητρον (LTr., WH, -θρον), -ου, τό
(< φοβέω), [in LXX: Is 19:17 (חָגָא) * ;]
that which causes fright, a terror: pl. (as always, exc. Is, l.c.), Lk 21:11 (Hipp., Plat.).†

φιλονεικία.as:
** φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: II Mac 4:4, IV Mac 1:268:26 * ;]
love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: Lk 22:24 (but v. Field, Notes, 75 f.).†

φραγέλλιον.sd: a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment
φραγέλλιον.der: neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417 (φραγελλόω);

φαῦλος.as:
φαῦλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX: Pr 22:8 (עַוְלָה) 29:9 (אֳבִיל), etc. ;]
slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (v. LS, s.v.), in NT, as freq. in cl., always with distinct moral reference (v. Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., lxxxiv), worthless, bad: Jo 3:20, Tit 2:8, Ja 3:16; opp. to ἀγαθός (q.v.), Jo 5:29, Ro 9:11, II Co 5:10.†
SYN.: v.s. ἄθεσμος

φοῖνιξ.as:
φοῖνιξ (on the accent, v. Bl., § 4, 2; WM, § 6, lc), -ικος, ὁ,
[in LXX for תָּמָר,תֹּמֶר,תִּמֹּרָה;]
the date-palm, palm: τὰ βαΐα τῶν φ., Jo 12:13; of palm branches, φοίνικες (as Arist., II Mac 10:7, al.), Re 7:9.†

φανός.as:
* φανός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< φαίνω),
a torch or lantern (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 131 f.): Jo 18:3.†
SYN.: v.s. λαμπάς

Φρυγία.long: Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor, the north-western part of which was in the Roman province Asia and the south-eastern part in the Roman province Galatia.
Φρυγία.sd: Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor
Φρυγία.as:
φρυγία, -ας, ἡ
(prop., the adj., Φρυγίος, -α, -ον; sc. γῆ, χώρα),
Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: Ac 2:10; Φ. καὶ Γαλατικὴ χώρα (Γ. χ. κ. Φ.), Ac 16:618:23 (on these phrases v. DB, i, 89 f.; CGT, Gal., xxii f.).†

φθέγγομαι.sd: to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim
φθέγγομαι.der: probably akin to G5338 (φέγγος) and thus to G5346 (φημί);
φθέγγομαι.as:
φθέγγομαι
[in LXX for ענה, נבע hi., etc. ;]
of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., Ac 4:18; seq. ἐν φωνῇ, II Pe 2:16; c. acc., ὑπέρογκα, ib. 18.†

φρυάσσω.long: I am wanton, insolent; I roar, rage.
φρυάσσω.sd: to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult
φρυάσσω.as:
† φρυάσσω
(so Ps, l.c., NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Ps 2:1 (רָגַשׁ), II Mac 7:34 R, III Mac 2:2 * ;]
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaph., to be wanton, insolent: Ac 4:25(LXX).†

φύλαξ.as:
φύλαξ, -ακος, ὁ
(< φυλάσσω), [in LXX for שָׁמַר, צוּר ;]
a guard, keeper: Ac 5:2312:6, 19.†

Φαραώ.long: Pharaoh, the title of ancient Egyptian kings.
Φαραώ.as:
Φαραώ, ὁ indecl.
(in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה),
Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: Ac 7:13, 21, Ro 9:17, He 11:24; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, Ac 7:10.†

Φοινίκη.long: Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.
Φοινίκη.sd: palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine
Φοινίκη.as:
φοινίκη, -ης, ἡ
Phœnicia: Ac 11:1915:321:2 (v. DB, iii, 856b, 857an).†

Φίλιπποι.long: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.
Φίλιπποι.as:
φίλιπποι, -ων, οἱ
(on the pl., v. WM, § 27, 3)
Philippi: Ac 16:1220:6, Phl 1:1, I Th 2:2.†

φιλόσοφος.sd: fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher"
φιλόσοφος.as:
φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Da LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), IV Mac 1:15:357:7 * ;]
a philosopher: Ac 17:18.†

φείδομαι.sd: to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently
φείδομαι.as:
φείδομαι
[in LXX for חמל, חוּס, חשׂךְ, etc. ;]
to spare: II Co 13:2; c. gen. pers., Ac 20:29, Ro 8:3211:21, I Co 7:28, II Co 1:23, II Pe 2:4, 5; c. inf., to forbear, II Co 12:6.†

φάσις.der: from G5346 (φημί) (not the same as "phase", which is from G5316 (φαίνω));
φάσις.as:
φάσις, -εως, ἡ
(< φαίνω), [in LXX: II Es 4:17, Da TH Su :55, IV Mac 15:25א1* ;]
information, esp. against fraud or other crime: Ac 21:31.†

Φῆλιξ.long: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52 ?) till A.D. 59.
Φῆλιξ.as:
φῆλιξ (L, Φή-), -ικος, ὁ
Felix, procurator of Judæa: Ac 23:24, 2624:3, 22, 24, 25, 2725:14.†

φάσκω.der: prolongation from the same as G5346 (φημί);
φάσκω.as:
φάσκω
[in LXX: Ge 26:20 (אמר), Da LXX Bel :8, II Mac 14:27, 14:32, III Mac 3:7 * ;]
to affirm, assert: c. acc. et inf., Ac 24:925:19; c. inf. et nom., Ro 1:22.†

Φῆστος.as:
φῆστος, -ου, ὁ
(Porcius), Festus, procurator of Judæa: Ac 24:2725:1ff.Ac 26:24, 25, 32.†

φαντασία.as:
φαντασία, -ας, ἡ
(< φαντάζω), [in LXX: Za 10:1 (חָזִיז), חֲזִיז), Hb 2:18, 193:10, Wi 18:17 * ;]
1. as philos. term,
(a)imagination;
(b) = φάντασμα (Plat., Arist.).
2. In later writers (Polyb., al.), show, display: Ac 25:23.†

φιλανθρώπως.der: adverb from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G444 (ἄνθρωπος);
φιλανθρώπως.as:
** φιλανθρώπως
adv.,
[in LXX: II Mac 9:27, III Mac 3:20 * ;]
humanely, kindly: Ac 27:3.†

Φοῖνιξ.long: Phoenix, a bay on the south coast of Crete.
Φοῖνιξ.as:
Φοῖνιξ, -ικος, ο, ἡ
(a)a Phœnician (also with fem., Φοίνισσα, Hom., al.);
(b)Phœnix, a city of Crete: Ac 27:12.†

φιλανθρωπία.as:
** φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Es 8:13, II Mac 6:2214:9, III Mac 3:15, 18 * ;]
humanity, kindness (v. Field, Notes, 147 f.): Ac 28:2, Tit 3:4 (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).†

φρύγανον.sd: akin to the base of G5395 (φλόξ)); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig
φρύγανον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of (to roast or parch;
φρύγανον.as:
φρύγανον, -ου, τό
(< φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל, etc. ;]
a dry stick: pl., brushwood: Ac 28:3.†

φιλοφρόνως.sd: with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly
φιλοφρόνως.as:
** φιλοφρόνως
(< φιλόφρων)
adv.,
[in LXX: II Mac 3:9, IV Mac 8:5 * ;]
kindly, with friendliness: Ac 28:7.†

Φόρον.sd: a forum or market-place; only in comparative with G675 (Ἄππιος); a station on the Appian road
Φόρον.as:
*† φόρον, -ου, τό
(Lat. forum): Ἀππίου Φ., v.s. Ἄππιος.

φθαρτός.as:
φθαρτός, -ή, -όν (φθείρω)
[in LXX: Le 22:25 (מִשְׁחָת), Is 54:17 Aא3, Wi 9:1514:8, II Mac 7:16 * ;]
perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, Ro 1:23 (opp. to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, I Co 9:25 (opp. to ἄφθαρτος); σπσρά, I Pe 1:23 (opp. to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, I Co 15:53, 54; pl., I Pe 1:18.†

φυσικός.long: natural, (a) according to nature, (b) merely animal.
φυσικός.as:
* φυσικός, -ή, -όν
(< φύσις),
natural
(a)produced by nature, innate (Xen., Arist., al.);
(b)according to nature (Arist., Diod., al.): opp. to παρὰ φύσιν, Ro 1:26, 27;
(c)governed by mere natural instinct (cf. Plut., Mor., 706A): ζῷα γεγεννημένα φ. (RV, born mere animals; Mayor, born creatures of instinct; ICC, animals born of mere nature), II Pe 2:12,†

φύσις.sd: growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage
φύσις.as:
** φύσις, -εως, ἡ
(< φύω) [in LXX: Wi 7:2013:119:20 אΑ, III Mac 3:29, IV Mac 1:205:7, 8, 2513:2715:13, 2516:3 * ;]
nature, i.e.,
(a) the nature (natural powers or constitution) of a person or thing: Ja 3:7, II Pe 1:4;
τέκνα φυσει ὀργῆς, Eph 2:3;
(b)origin, birth (Soph., Xen., al.): Ro 2:27, Ga 2:15;
(c)nature, i.e. the regular order or law of nature: I Co 11:14; dat., φύσει adverbially, by nature, Ro 2:14, Ga 4:8; παρὰ φύσιν, against nature, Ro 1:2611:24; καρὰ φ., according to nature, naturally, Ro 11:21, 24.†

φράσσω.sd: to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence)
φράσσω.der: apparently a strengthening form of the base of G5424 (φρήν);
φράσσω.as:
φράσσω
[in LXX: Jb 38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Ho 2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pr 21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;]
to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, He 11:33; στόμα, metaph., Ro 3:19; pass., καύχησις, II Co 11:10.†

φρόνημα.as:
** φρόνημα, -τος, τό
(< φρονέω), [in LXX: II Mac 7:2113:9 * ;]
that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 86), the thought: Ro 8:6, 7, 27.†

φθορά.sd: decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively)
φθορά.as:
φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc. ;]
destruction, corruption, decay (v. Mayor on II Pe, App.,175 ff.): Ro 8:21, I Co 15:42, Col 2:22, II Pe 2:12; opp. to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, Ga 6:8; by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, I Co 15:50; of moral decay, II Pe 1:42:12, 19 (cf. Wi 14:12).†

φύραμα.long: a mass or lump, as of bread dough.
φύραμα.sd: perhaps akin to G5453 (φύω) through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough
φύραμα.der: from a prolonged form of (to mix a liquid with a solid;
φύραμα.as:
φύραμα, -τος, τό
(< φυράω, to mix), [in LXX: Ex 8:3 (7:28) 12:34 (משארת), Nu 15:20, 21 (עריסה) * ;]
that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump: of dough, Ro 11:16, I Co 5:6, 7, Ga 5:9; of clay, Ro 9:21.†

φθόγγος.sd: utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental)
φθόγγος.as:
φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ
(< φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Ps 18 (19):4 (קַו), Wi 19:18 * ;]
a sound: Ro 10:18(LXX)I Co 14:7.†

φιλαδελφία.long: brotherly love, love of Christian brethren.
φιλαδελφία.kj: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren
φιλαδελφία.as:
φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: IV Mac 13:23, 2614:1 * ;]
the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (v.s. ἀδελφός), Ro 12:10, I Th 4:9, He 13:1, I Pe 1:22, II Pe 1:7.†

φιλόστοργος.sd: fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian
φιλόστοργος.der: from G5384 (φίλος) and (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children);
φιλόστοργος.as:
** φιλόστοργος, -ον
(< στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:13 * ;]
tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Ro 12:10.†

φιλοξενία.as:
* φιλο-ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλόξενος),
love of strangers, hospitality: Ro 12:13, He 13:2.†

φιλοτιμέομαι.long: I am zealous, strive eagerly, desire very strongly.
φιλοτιμέομαι.sd: to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something)
φιλοτιμέομαι.der: middle voice from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G5092 (τιμή);
φιλοτιμέομαι.as:
** φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(< φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:35 A ;]
to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): c. inf., Ro 15:20, II Co 5:9, I Th 4:11.†

Φοίβη.long: Phoebe, a Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae.
Φοίβη.sd: probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς)); Phœbe, a Christian woman
Φοίβη.as:
φοίβη, -ης, ἡ
Phœbe, a deaconess of Cenchræa: Ro 16:1.†

Φλέγων.der: active participle of the base of G5395 (φλόξ);

Φιλόλογος.sd: fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian

φθείρω.sd: properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave)
φθείρω.der: probably strengthened from (to pine or waste);
φθείρω.as:
φθείρω
[in LXX chiefly for שׁחת hi., pi., also for חבל, etc. ;]
to destroy, corrupt, spoil (on the varied usage and distinctive meaning of the word, v. Mayor on II Pe, App., 175 ff.): c. acc., I Co 3:1715:23, II Co 7:2; seq. ἀπό, II Co 11:3; ἐν, II Pe 2:12, Ju 10, Re 19:2; κατά, Eph 4:22 (cf. δια-, κατα-φθείρω).†

φυσιόω.long: I inflate, puff up; pass: I am puffed up, arrogant, proud.
φυσιόω.der: from G5449 (φύσις) in the primary sense of blowing;
φυσιόω.as:
*† φυσιόω, -ῶ
(< φῦσα, bellows), = cl. φυσάω,
to puff or blow up, inflate. Metaph., to puff up, make proud: I Co 8:1. Pass., to be puffed up with pride: I Co 4:18, 195:213:4; seq. ὑπό, Col 2:18; seq. ὑπὲρ . . . κατά, I Co 4:6 (on the form of the subjc., v. M, Pr., 54; Bl., § 22, 3).†

φιλόνεικος.sd: probably akin to G3534 (νῖκος)); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious
φιλόνεικος.as:
φιλό-νεικος, -ον
(< νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Ez 3:7 (מֵצַח־חָזָק)* ;]
fond of strife, contentious: I Co 11:16.†

φανέρωσις.sd: exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment
φανέρωσις.as:
† φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< φανερόω), [in LXX as v.l. for δήλωσιςאוּרִים), Le 8:8, Cod. Ven. (Thayer, s.v.) * ;]
manifestation: I Co 12:7, II Co 4:2.†

φρήν.sd: the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties)
φρήν.der: probably from an obsolete (to rein in or curb; compare G5420 (φράσσω));
φρήν.as:
φρήν gen., φρενός, ἡ,
[in LXX most freq. in Pr (6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also III Mac 4:165:47 ;]
chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.;
1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff.
2.heart, mind, thought: pl., I Co 14:20 (v. Edwards, Eng.-Gr.Lex., App., 1).†

Φορτουνᾶτος.as:
φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, v. Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ
(Lat.) Fortunatus: I Co 16:17 (v. Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†

φωτισμός.as:
φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(φωτίζω) [in LXX: Jb 3:9, Ps 26 (27):143 (44):377 (78):14138 (139):11 (אוֹר), Ps 89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;]
illumination, light: metaph., I Co 4:4, 6.†

φρουρέω.long: I guard, keep, as by a military guard.
φρουρέω.sd: to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect
φρουρέω.der: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G3708 (ὁράω);
φρουρέω.as:
φρουρέω, -ῶ
(< φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Es 4:56, Jth 3:6, Wi 17:16, I Mac 11:3 * ;]
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: II Co 11:32; metaph., Ga 3:23, Phl 4:7, I Pe 1:5.†

φυσίωσις.as:
*† φυσίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< φυσιόω),
a puffing up, swelling with pride: pl., II Co 12:20.†

φαρμακεία.sd: medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively)

φθονέω.as:
** φθονέω, -ῶ
(< φθόνος), [in LXX: To 4:7, 16 AB * ;]
to envy: c. dat. (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., acc.), as in cl., Ga 5:26.†

φρεναπατάω.long: I deceive the mind, impose upon.
φρεναπατάω.sd: to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude
φρεναπατάω.as:
*† φρεν-απατάω, -ῶ
(< φρεναπάτης),
to deceive one's mind (Lft., deceive by fancies, v. Ga., l.c.): c. acc. pers., Ga 6:3.†

φωστήρ.long: a light, an illuminator, perhaps the sun; a star; brilliancy.
φωστήρ.sd: an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy
φωστήρ.as:
φωστήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(< φῶς), [in LXX: Ge 1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Da LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Es 8:79, Wi 13:2, Si 43:7 * ;]
a luminary, light: Phl 2:15, Re 21:11.†
SYN.: φέγγος, φῶς

Φιλιππήσιος.long: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.
Φιλιππήσιος.sd: a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi
Φιλιππήσιος.as:
φιλιππήσιος, -ου, ὁ
(for other forms in use, v. Lft., in l.)
a Philippian: Phl 4:15.†

φιλοσοφία.long: love of wisdom, philosophy, in the NT of traditional Jewish theology.
φιλοσοφία.as:
** Φιλο-σοφία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλόσοφος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:15:10, 227:9, 21 * ;]
the love and pursuit of wisdom; hence, philosophy, investi­gation of truth and nature: of the so-called philosophy of false teachers, Col 2:8 (v. Lft., ICC, in l.).†

φιλόξενος.as:
* φιλό-ξενος, -ον
loving strangers, hospitable: I Ti 3:2, Tit 1:8, I Pe 4:9.†

φλύαρος.as:
** φλύαρος, -ον
(< φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: IV Mac 5:10 * ;]
babbling, garrulous: I Ti 5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, IV Mac, l.c.).†

φιλαργυρία.as:
* φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ
(< φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:262:15א1 * ;]
love of money, avarice: I Ti 6:1.†
SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (v. Tr., Syn., § xxiv).

Φύγελος.long: Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia who deserted Paul.

Φίλητος.sd: amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity

φίλαυτος.as:
* φίλ-αυτος, -ον
loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: II Ti 3:2.†
SYN.: αὐθάδης (v. Tr., Syn., § xciii)

φιλήδονος.as:
*† φιλήδονος, -ον
(φίλος, ἡδονή),
loving pleasure: II Ti 3:4 (Polyb., Plut. al.).†

φαιλόνης.der: by transposition for a derivative probably of G5316 (φαίνω) (as showing outside the other garments);

φιλάγαθος.sd: fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue
φιλάγαθος.as:
** φιλ-άγαθος, -ον
[in LXX: Wi 7:22 * ;]
loving that which is good, loving goodness: Tit 1:8 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

φρεναπάτης.as:
*† φρεναπάτης, -ου, ὁ
(< φρήν, ἀπάτη),
a deceiver (B1., deceiver of his own mind, § 28, 52, where v. ref. to π.): Tit 1:10 (eccl.).†

φίλανδρος.sd: fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife
φίλανδρος.as:
* φίλανδρος, -ον
1.loving men (Æsch.).
2. Of a wife, loving her husband (freq. in epitaphs, v. LS, s.v., Deiss., BS, 255): Tit 2:4.†

φιλότεκνος.sd: fond of one's children, i.e. maternal
φιλότεκνος.as:
** φιλότεκνος, -ον
(< φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:4-6 * ;]
loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, q.v., Tit 2:4.†

φροντίζω.long: I am thoughtful, careful, give heed.
φροντίζω.sd: to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious
φροντίζω.as:
φροντίζω
(< φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: I Ki 9:5 (דָּאַג), Ps 39 (40):17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;]
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., c acc., c. gen.), c. inf., Tit 3:8 (v. Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†

Φιλήμων.long: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.

φοβερός.as:
φοβερός, -ά, -όν
(< φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for נוֺרָא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם ;]
fearful, whether act, or pass.;
1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible(LXX): He 10:27, 3112:21
2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).†

φαντάζομαι.long: I cause to appear, make visible.
φαντάζομαι.sd: to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle)
φαντάζομαι.as:
** φαντάζω
(< φαίνω) [in LXX: Wi 6:16, Si 31 (34):5* ;]
to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., He 12:21.†

φρίσσω.as:
φρίσσω
(Att.. -ττω, and so IV Mac 14:917:7) [in LXX: Jb 4:15 (סמר pi.), etc. ;]
1.to be rough, bristle.
2.to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Ja 2:19 (v. Hort, in l.).†

φλογίζω.long: I inflame, fire with passion, set on fire, burn up.
φλογίζω.sd: to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion)
φλογίζω.as:
φλογίζω
(< φλόξ), [in LXX: Ex 9:24 (לקח hith.), Nu 21:14 (†), Ps 96 (97):3 (להט pi.), Da TH 3:27(94) (חֲרַךְ ithp.), Si 3:30, I Mac 3:5 * ;]
to set on fire, burn, burn up: fig., Ja 3:6 (on the meaning of the sentence, v. Hort, in l.).†

φιλία.as:
φιλία, -ας, ἡ
(< φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה ;]
friendship: c. gen. obj., Ja 4:4.†

φιλάδελφος.long: loving like a brother, loving one's brethren.
φιλάδελφος.as:
* φιλ-άδελφος, -ον
[in LXX: II Mac 15:14, IV Mac 13:2115:10 * ;]
loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), I Pe 3:8.†

φωσφόρος.as:
* φωσ-φόρος, -ον
(< φῶς, φέρω),
light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Is 14:12, Jb 3:9, Ps 110:3): metaph., II Pe 1:19 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

φιλοπρωτεύω.long: I love the chief place, desire preeminence.
φιλοπρωτεύω.sd: to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction
φιλοπρωτεύω.der: from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G4413 (πρῶτος);
φιλοπρωτεύω.as:
*† φιλοπρωτεύω
(< φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.)
to strive to be first: III Jo 9 (eccl.).†

φλυαρέω.long: I gossip against, talk idly, make empty charges against, talk nonsense.
φλυαρέω.sd: to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously
φλυαρέω.as:
* φλυαρέω, -ῶ
(< φλύαρος),
to talk nonsense: c. acc. pers., ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jo 10.†

φθινοπωρινός.long: autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected.
φθινοπωρινός.sd: akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω)) and G3703 (ὀπώρα) (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves)
φθινοπωρινός.as:
* φθιν-οπωρινός, -ή, -όν
(< φθινόπωρον, late autumn),
autumnal: δένδρα φ., autumn trees (said to be without fruit therefore at a time when fruit might be expected; v. Mayor's elaborate note, Ep. Ju., 55-59, and reff. there): Ju 12.†

Φιλαδέλφεια.long: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia.
Φιλαδέλφεια.sd: Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor
Φιλαδέλφεια.der: from (the same as G5361 (φιλάδελφος)), a king of Pergamos;
Φιλαδέλφεια.as:
Φιλαδελφία (Rec. -έλφεια), -ας, ἡ
Philadelphia, a city of Lydia: Re 1:113:7.†

φιάλη.as:
φιάλη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for מִזְרָק ;]
a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations, etc.: Re 5:815:716:1-1717:121:9.†

φάρμακον.as:
φάρμακον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX for כֶּשֶׁף ;]
(a)a drug;
(b)an in­cantation, enchantment: Re 9:21, Tr., mg., WH, txt. (RV, sorceries).†

φάρμακος.as:
φαρμακός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for מְכַשֵׁף, etc. ;]
devoted to magical arts. As subst., ὁ φ. = φαρμακεύς, a magician, sorcerer: Re 21:822:15.†
